subject: HealthSync private offer — activation roadmap & term clarification
messages:
From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@healthsync.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: 2026-11-27T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify term length & buyer approvals for AWS private offer

Irene — thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of quick follow-ups from procurement and legal as we prepare to route the private offer through AWS Marketplace: 

1) Term length: Legal is pushing back on anything > 12 months without an auto-termination clause tied to usage thresholds. Can Redwood split the two-year pricing into a 12-month firm commitment + optional extension for year two?

2) Buyer approvals: Procurement wants a short checklist of who needs to sign off on the AWS private offer (finance, procurement, security) and whether DocuSign is acceptable or we need a PO first. 

3) Activation timing: They want to know how quickly the private offer appears in their AWS account after signature (hours? days?), and what the activation window is for the buyer to accept the offer.

Attached is our internal procurement checklist (we'll share the PO once legal signs). Can you confirm and send a version of the PO we can use for review?

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Procurement
HealthSync

attachment: HealthSync_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Chen <tom.chen@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify term length & buyer approvals for AWS private offer

Tom — really helpful list, thanks. Quick answers inline below and a proposed activation roadmap attached. High level: we can support a 12-month firm commitment with an optional 12-month extension at the same pricing (no automatic charge without explicit acceptance). That tends to satisfy legal while keeping marketplace activation simple.

1) Term length
- Proposal: 12-month firm + 12-month optional extension (Customer must accept extension before the start of year 2). We can also offer a mid-term pro-rata true-up if usage exceeds committed units by >20%.

2) Buyer approvals
- Checklist we typically see: 
  - Procurement (formal approval)
  - Finance/CFO (budget confirmation)
  - Security point-of-contact (for the activation evidence pack)
- DocuSign is acceptable for Redwood (common). If you require a PO before we submit the private offer, we can accept that and stage the offer submission once PO is received.

3) Activation timing
- From Redwood side: once the private offer is submitted and accepted by AWS (automated), buyers typically see the offer in their AWS console within 2–4 hours. In edge cases (manual review by AWS) it can take 24 hours.
- Offer acceptance window: we recommend a 30-day acceptance window for buyers to complete. We can shorten if your procurement needs faster signoff.

Attached: 1) HealthSync_PO_Draft_v2.pdf (our draft private offer/ordering doc) 2) Activation_Roadmap.pdf (step-by-step flow for signing and AWS activation).

Next steps: I'll loop Ben (billing/POs) and Neha (security evidence) for any outstanding items. If Procurement can confirm they are comfortable with DocuSign + optional extension semantics, we'll prepare the final PO/DocuSign packet for legal review.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive — Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Tom/Irene — adding finance/billing notes here. A few pragmatic details from our side to make procurement smooth: 

- If you provide a PO before we submit to AWS, please include the deal_id (HS-22073) and the billing contact/email. We will stage the private offer submission in Seller Central using the PO as the evidence/trigger if you prefer.
- If you want immediate activation after signature, choose DocuSign + electronic acceptance path — we can submit the private offer to AWS same day once we have the signed DocuSign packet and the buyer email for acceptance. 
- Invoices are generated monthly based on usage against the committed units. If you need fixed prepayment invoicing, flag that now and we'll review via finance.

Also, Neha — can you confirm the minimum evidence pack we should attach to the private offer for HealthSync's security team (SOC 2 summary, data retention note, and a short runbook)?

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@healthsync.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com, Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify term length & buyer approvals for AWS private offer

Irene/Ben — appreciated and that helps a lot. Procurement and legal talked this morning and agree to the 12-month firm + optional 12-month extension approach. They also confirm DocuSign is acceptable as long as the PO number is included on the DocuSign cover letter. 

Two quick asks before we push to legal signature: 
1) Can Redwood include the SOC 2 summary and retention note in the DocuSign package so our security team can sign off concurrently?
2) Please set the acceptance window to 21 days instead of 30 — procurement prefers a shorter window.

If you can update the PO draft with those two items, we'll route to legal today and aim to return a signed DocuSign by Friday. Feel free to call if anything blocks.

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Procurement, HealthSync
